10-1-1: - Statutory Authorization, Findings of Fact, Purpose, and Objectives
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-1STAUFIFAPUOB","Title":"10-1-1: - Statutory Authorization, Findings of Fact, Purpose, and Objectives","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Statutory Authority: The Legislature of the State of Idaho, pursuant to Idaho Code\n sections 46-1020, 46-1023, and 46-1024, authorizes local governments to adopt floodplain\n management ordinances that identify floodplains and minimum floodplain development\n standards to minimize flood hazards and protect human life, health, and property.\n Therefore, the Council of the City of Star Idaho does hereby ordain as follows.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Findings of Fact:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The flood hazard areas of the City of Star are subject to periodic inundation that\n results in:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Loss of life and property;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Health and safety hazards;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Disruption of commerce and governmental services;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Extraordinary public expenditures for flood relief and protection; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Impairment of the tax base, all of which adversely affect the public health, safety,\n and general welfare.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n These flood losses are caused by development in flood hazard areas, which are inadequately\n elevated, flood-proofed, or otherwise unprotected from flood damages, and by the cumulative\n effect of obstructions in floodplains causing increases in flood heights and velocities.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Local government units have the primary responsibility for planning, adopting, and\n enforcing land use regulations to accomplish proper floodplain management.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Statement of Purpose: The purpose of this chapter is to promote public health, safety,\n and general welfare and to minimize public and private losses due to flood conditions\n in specific areas by provisions designed to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Protect human life, health, and property;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimize damage to public facilities and utilities such as water purification and\n sewage treatment plants, water and gas mains, electric, telephone and sewer lines,\n streets, and bridges located in floodplains;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Help maintain a stable tax base by providing for the sound use and development of\n flood prone areas;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimize expenditure of public money for costly flood control projects;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimize the need for rescue and emergency services associated with flooding, generally\n undertaken at the expense of the general public;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimize prolonged business interruptions;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Ensure potential buyers are notified the property is in an area of special flood hazard;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Ensure those who occupy the areas of special flood hazard assume responsibility for\n their actions; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Participate in and maintain eligibility for flood insurance disaster relief.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Objectives and Methods of Reducing Flood Losses: In order to accomplish its purpose,\n this chapter includes methods and provisions to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Require that development which is vulnerable to floods, including structures and facilities\n necessary for the general health, safety, and welfare of citizens, be protected against\n flood damage at the time of initial construction;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Restrict or prohibit developments which are dangerous to health, safety, and property\n due to water or erosion hazards, or which increase flood heights, velocities, or erosion;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Control filling, grading, dredging, and other development which may increase flood\n damage or erosion;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Prevent or regulate the construction of flood barriers that will unnaturally divert\n flood waters or that may increase flood hazards to other lands; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Preserve and restore natural floodplains, stream channels, and natural protective\n barriers which carry and store flood waters.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021)\n

10-1-2: - Definitions
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-2DE","Title":"10-1-2: - Definitions","Content":"
\n

\n Unless specifically defined below, words or phrases used in this chapter shall be\n interpreted according to the meaning they have in common usage and to give this chapter\n it's most reasonable application.\n

\n

\n ACCESSORY STRUCTURE (APPURTENANT STRUCTURE): A structure on the same lot or parcel\n as a principal structure, the use of which is incidental and subordinate to the principal\n structure.\n

\n

\n ADDITION (TO AN EXISTING BUILDING): An extension or increase in the floor area or\n height of a building or structure.\n

\n

\n APPEAL: A request for review of the Floodplain Administrator's interpretation of provisions\n of this chapter or request for a variance.\n

\n

\n AREA OF SHALLOW FLOODING: A designated AO, AH, AR/AO, or AR/AH zone on a community's\n Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) with a one percent (1%) or greater annual chance of\n flooding to an average depth of one to three feet (1' - 3') where a clearly defined\n channel does not exist, where the path of flooding is unpredictable, and where velocity\n flow may be evident. Such flooding is characterized by ponding or sheet flow.\n

\n

\n AREA OF SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD: See SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD AREA (SFHA).\n

\n

\n BASE FLOOD: The flood having a one percent (1%) chance of being equaled or exceeded\n in any given year.\n

\n

\n BASE FLOOD ELEVATION (BFE): A determination by the Federal Insurance Administrator\n of the water surface elevations of the base flood, that is, the flood level that has\n a one percent (1%) or greater chance of occurrence in any given year. When the BFE\n has not been provided in a special flood hazard area, it may be obtained from engineering\n studies available from a Federal, State, or other source using FEMA-approved engineering\n methodologies. This elevation, when combined with the freeboard, establishes the flood\n protection elevation.\n

\n

\n BASEMENT: Any area of the building having its floor sub grade (below ground level)\n on all sides.\n

\n

\n BUILDING: See STRUCTURE.\n

\n

\n CRITICAL FACILITIES: Facilities that are vital to flood response activities or critical\n to the health and safety of the public before, during, and after a flood, such as\n a hospital, emergency operations center, electric substation, police station, fire\n station, nursing home, school, vehicle and equipment storage facility, or shelter;\n and facilities that, if flooded, would make the flood problem and its impacts much\n worse, such as a hazardous materials facility, power generation facility, water utility,\n or wastewater treatment plant.\n

\n

\n DATUM: The vertical datum is a base measurement point (or set of points) from which\n all elevations are determined. Historically, that common set of points was the National\n Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929 (NGVD29). The vertical datum currently adopted by\n the federal government as a basis for measuring heights is the North American Vertical\n Datum of 1988 (NAVD88).\n

\n

\n DEVELOPMENT: Any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including\n but not limited to buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading,\n paving, excavation or drilling operations, or storage of equipment or materials.\n

\n

\n DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITY: Any activity defined as development which will necessitate a\n floodplain development permit; such as the construction of buildings, structures,\n or accessory structures; additions or substantial improvements to existing structures;\n bulkheads, retaining walls, piers, and pools; the placement of mobile homes; or the\n deposition or extraction of materials; the construction or elevation of dikes, berms\n and levees.\n

\n

\n DIGITAL FLOOD INSURANCE RATE MAP (DFIRM): The digital official map of a community,\n issued by the Federal Insurance Administrator, on which both the special flood hazard\n areas and the risk premium zones applicable to the community are delineated.\n

\n

\n ELEVATED BUILDING: For insurance purposes, a non-basement building which has its lowest\n elevated floor raised above ground level by foundation walls, shear walls, posts,\n piers, pilings, or columns.\n

\n

\n ELEVATION CERTIFICATE: The elevation certificate is an important administrative tool\n of the NFIP. It is used to determine the proper flood insurance premium rate; it is\n used to document elevation information; and it may be used to support a request for\n a letter of map amendment (LOMA) or letter of map revision based on fill (LOMR-F).\n

\n

\n ENCLOSURE: An area enclosed by solid walls below the BFE/FPE or an area formed when\n any space below the BFE/FPE is enclosed on all sides by walls or partitions. Insect\n screening or open wood lattice used to surround space below the BFE/RFPE is not considered\n an enclosure.\n

\n

\n ENCROACHMENT: The advance or infringement of uses, fill, excavation, buildings, structures,\n or development into a floodplain, which may impede or alter the flow capacity of a\n floodplain.\n

\n

\n ELEVATED BUILDING: For insurance purposes, a non-basement building which has its lowest\n elevated floor raised above ground level by foundation walls, shear walls, posts,\n piers, pilings, or columns.\n

\n

\n ELEVATION CERTIFICATE: The elevation certificate is an important administrative tool\n of the NFIP. It is used to determine the proper flood insurance premium rate; it is\n used to document elevation information; and it may be used to support a request for\n a letter of map amendment (LOMA) or letter of map revision based on fill (LOMR-F).\n

\n

\n EXISTING CONSTRUCTION: For the purposes of determining rates, structures for which\n the \"start of construction\" commenced before the effective date of the FIRM or before\n January 1, 1975, for FIRMs effective before that date. \"Existing construction\" may\n also be referred to as \"existing structures.\"\n

\n

\n EXISTING MANUFACTURED HOME PARK OR MANUFACTURED HOME SUBDIVISION: A manufactured home\n park or subdivision where the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on\n which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including, at a minimum, the installation\n of utilities, the construction of streets, and final site grading or the pouring of\n concrete pads) is completed before the effective date of the original floodplain management\n regulations adopted by the community, on September 6, 2002.\n

\n

\n EXISTING STRUCTURES: See EXISTING CONSTRUCTION.\n

\n

\n EXPANSION TO AN EXISTING MANUFACTURED HOME PARK OR SUBDIVISION: The preparation of\n additional sites by the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which\n the manufacturing homes are to be affixed (including the installation of utilities,\n the construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete\n pads).\n

\n

\n FLOOD OR FLOODING:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A general and temporary condition of partial or complete inundation of normally dry\n land areas from:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The overflow of inland or tidal waters.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters from any source.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Mudslides (i.e., mudflows) which are proximately caused by flooding as defined in\n subsection A2 of this definition and are akin to a river of liquid and flowing mud\n on the surfaces of normally dry land areas, as when earth is carried by a current\n of water and deposited along the path of the current.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The collapse or subsidence of land along the shore of a lake or other body of water\n as a result of erosion or undermining caused by waves or currents of water exceeding\n anticipated cyclical levels or suddenly caused by an unusually high water level in\n a natural body of water, accompanied by a severe storm, or by an unanticipated force\n of nature, such as flash flood or an abnormal tidal surge, or by some similarly unusual\n and unforeseeable event which results in flooding as defined in subsection A1 of this\n definition.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n FLOOD BOUNDARY AND FLOODWAY MAP (FBFM): The FBFM shows how the floodplain is divided\n into the floodway and flood fringe where streams are studied in detail. They also\n show general floodplain areas where floodplains have been studied by approximate methods.\n

\n

\n FLOOD ELEVATION DETERMINATION: See BASE FLOOD ELEVATION (BFE).\n

\n

\n FLOOD ELEVATION STUDY: See FLOOD INSURANCE STUDY (FIS).\n

\n

\n FLOOD HAZARD BOUNDARY MAP (FHBM): An official map of a community, issued by the Federal\n Insurance Administrator, where the boundaries of the flood, mudslide (i.e., mudflow)\n related erosion areas having special hazards have been designated as Zones A, M, and/or\n E.\n

\n

\n FLOOD INSURANCE RATE MAP (FIRM): An official map of a community, on which the Federal\n Insurance Administrator has delineated both the special flood hazard areas and the\n risk premium zones applicable to the community. A FIRM that has been made available\n digitally is called a Digital Flood Insurance Rate Map (DFIRM).\n

\n

\n FLOOD INSURANCE STUDY (FIS): An examination, evaluation, and determination of flood\n hazards and, if appropriate, corresponding water surface elevations; or an examination,\n evaluation and determination of mudslide (i.e., mudflow) and/or flood-related erosion\n hazards.\n

\n

\n FLOODPLAIN OR FLOOD-PRONE AREA: Any land area susceptible to being inundated by water\n from any source (see definition of FLOODING).\n

\n

\n FLOODPLAIN ADMINISTRATOR: The individual appointed to administer and enforce the floodplain\n management regulations.\n

\n

\n FLOODPLAIN DEVELOPMENT PERMIT: Any type of permit that is required in conformance\n with the provisions of this chapter, prior to the commencement of any development\n activity.\n

\n

\n FLOODPLAIN MANAGEMENT: The operation of an overall program of corrective and preventive\n measures for reducing flood damage, including but not limited to emergency preparedness\n plans, flood control works, and flood plain management regulations.\n

\n

\n FLOODPLAIN MANAGEMENT REGULATIONS: Zoning ordinances, subdivision regulations, building\n codes, health regulations, special purpose ordinances (such as a floodplain ordinance,\n grading ordinance, and erosion control ordinance), and other applications of police\n power. The term describes such state or local regulations, in any combination thereof,\n which provide standards for the purpose of flood damage prevention and reduction.\n

\n

\n FLOODPROOFING: Any combination of structural and non-structural additions, changes,\n or adjustments to structures which reduce or eliminate flood damage to real estate\n or improved real property, water and sanitary facilities, structures and their contents.\n

\n

\n FLOOD PROTECTION ELEVATION (FPE): The base flood elevation plus the freeboard.\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In special flood hazard areas where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined,\n this elevation shall be the BFE plus two feet (2') of freeboard; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In special flood hazard areas where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall\n be at least two feet (2') above the highest adjacent grade.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n FLOOD PROTECTION SYSTEM: Those physical structural works for which funds have been\n authorized, appropriated, and expended and which have been constructed specifically\n to modify flooding in order to reduce the extent of the area within a community subject\n to a special flood hazard and the extent of the depths of associated flooding. Such\n a system typically includes dams, reservoirs, levees, or dikes. These specialized\n flood modifying works are those constructed in conformance with sound engineering\n standards.\n

\n

\n FLOODWAY: The channel of a river or other watercourse and the adjacent land areas\n that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing\n the water surface elevation more than a designated height.\n

\n

\n FLOOD ZONE: A geographical area shown on a flood hazard boundary map (FHBM) or flood\n insurance rate map (FIRM) that reflects the severity or type of flooding in the area,\n and applicable insurance rate.\n

\n

\n FREEBOARD: A factor of safety usually expressed in feet above a flood level for the\n purposes of floodplain management. Freeboard tends to compensate for the many unknown\n factors that could contribute to flood heights greater than the height calculated\n for a selected size flood and floodway conditions, such as wave action, obstructed\n bridge openings, debris and ice jams, and the hydrologic effects of urbanization in\n a watershed. The base flood elevation (BFE) plus the freeboard establishes the flood\n protection elevation (FPE).\n

\n

\n FUNCTIONALLY DEPENDENT USE: A use that cannot perform its intended purpose unless\n it is located or carried out in close proximity to water, such as a docking or port\n facility necessary for the loading and unloading of cargo or passengers, shipbuilding,\n or ship repair facilities. The term does not include long-term storage, manufacture,\n sales, or service facilities.\n

\n

\n HIGHEST ADJACENT GRADE (HAG): The highest natural elevation of the ground surface\n prior to construction, adjacent to the proposed walls of a structure. Refer to the\n FEMA Elevation Certificate for HAG related to building elevation information.\n

\n

\n HISTORIC STRUCTURE: A structure that is:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Listed individually in the National Register of Historic Places (a listing maintained\n by the U.S. Department of Interior) or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of\n the Interior as meeting the requirements for individual listing on the National Register;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Certified or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the Interior as contributing\n to the historical significance of a registered historic district or to a district\n preliminarily determined by the Secretary to qualify as a registered historic district;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Individually listed on a state inventory of historic places and determined as eligible\n by states with historic preservation programs which have been approved by the Secretary\n of the Interior; or\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Individually listed on a local inventory of historic places and determined as eligible\n by communities with historic preservation programs that have been certified either:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n By an approved state program as determined by the Secretary of the Interior; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Directly by the Secretary of the Interior in states without approved programs.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n LETTER OF MAP CHANGE (LOMC): A general term used to refer to the several types of\n revisions and amendments to FIRMs that can be accomplished by letter. They include\n Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA), Letter of Map Revision (LOMR), and Letter of Map Revision\n based on Fill (LOMR-F).\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n LETTER OF MAP AMENDMENT (LOMA): An official amendment, by letter, to an effective\n National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) map. A LOMA establishes a property's or structure's\n location in relation to the special flood hazard area (SFHA). LOMAs are usually issued\n because a property or structure has been inadvertently mapped as being in the floodplain\n but is actually on natural high ground above the base flood elevation.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n LETTER OF MAP REVISION (LOMR): FEMA's modification to an effective Flood Insurance\n Rate Map (FIRM) or a Flood Boundary and Floodway Map (FBFM) or both. LOMRs are generally\n based on the implementation of physical measures that affect the hydrologic or hydraulic\n characteristics of a flooding source and thus result in the modification of the existing\n regulatory floodway, the effective base flood elevations (BFEs), or the special flood\n hazard area (SFHA). The LOMR officially revises the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM)\n or Flood Boundary and Floodway Map (FBFM), and sometimes the Flood Insurance Study\n (FIS) report, and when appropriate, includes a description of the modifications. The\n LOMR is generally accompanied by an annotated copy of the affected portions of the\n FIRM, FBFM, or FIS report.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n LETTER OF MAP REVISION BASED ON FILL (LOMR-F): FEMA's modification of the Special\n Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) shown on the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) based on the\n placement of fill outside the existing regulatory floodway. The LOMR-F does not change\n the FIRM, FBFM, or FIS report.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n CONDITIONAL LETTER OF MAP REVISION (CLOMR): A formal review and comment as to whether\n a proposed flood protection project or other project complies with the minimum NFIP\n requirements for such projects with respect to delineation of special flood hazard\n areas. A CLOMR does not revise the effective Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) or Flood\n Insurance Study (FIS). Upon submission and approval of certified as-built documentation,\n a Letter of Map Revision (LOMR) may be issued by FEMA to revise the effective FIRM.\n Building permits and/or flood development permits cannot be issued based on a CLOMR,\n because a CLOMR does not change the NFIP map.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n LEVEE: A man-made structure, usually an earthen embankment, designed and constructed\n according to sound engineering practices, to contain, control, or divert the flow\n of water so as to provide protection from temporary flooding.\n

\n

\n LEVEE SYSTEM: A flood protection system that consists of a levee, or levees, and associated\n structures, such as closure and drainage devices, which are constructed and operated\n in accordance with sound engineering practices.\n

\n

\n LOWEST ADJACENT GRADE (LAG): The lowest point of the ground level next to the structure.\n Refer to the FEMA Elevation Certificate for LAG related to building elevation information.\n

\n

\n LOWEST FLOOR: The lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area (including basement). An\n unfinished or flood resistant enclosure, usable solely for parking of vehicles, building\n access or storage in an area other than a basement area is not considered a building's\n lowest floor; provided, that such enclosure is not built so as to render the structure\n in violation of the applicable non-elevation design requirements of 44 CFR § 60.3\n and this chapter.\n

\n

\n MANUFACTURED HOME: A structure, transportable in one or more sections, built on a\n permanent chassis and designed to be used with or without a permanent foundation when\n connected to the required utilities. The term \"Manufactured Home\" does not include\n a recreational vehicle.\n

\n

\n MANUFACTURED HOME PARK OR SUBDIVISION: A parcel (or contiguous parcels) of land divided\n into two (2) or more manufactured home lots for rent or sale.\n

\n

\n MARKET VALUE: The building value, not including the land value and that of any accessory\n structures or other improvements on the lot. Market value may be established by independent\n certified appraisal; replacement cost depreciated for age of building and quality\n of construction (Actual Cash Value); or adjusted tax assessed values.\n

\n

\n MEAN SEA LEVEL: For purposes of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), the National\n Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) of 1929 or other datum (such as North America Vertical\n Datum of 1988 - NAVD88) to which base flood elevations (BFEs) shown on a community's\n FIRM are referenced.\n

\n

\n MUDSLIDE (I.E., MUDFLOW): Describes a condition where there is a river, flow, or inundation\n of liquid mud down a hillside usually as a result of a dual condition of loss of brush\n cover and the subsequent accumulation of water on the ground preceded by a period\n of unusually heavy or sustained rain. A mudslide (i.e., mudflow) may occur as a distinct\n phenomenon while a landslide is in progress and will be recognized as such by the\n Administrator only if the mudflow, and not the landslide, is the proximate cause of\n damage that occurs.\n

\n

\n MUDSLIDE (I.E., MUDFLOW) AREA MANAGEMENT: The operation of an overall program of corrective\n and preventive measures for reducing mudslide (i.e., mudflow) damage, including but\n not limited to emergency preparedness plans, mudslide control works, and flood plain\n management regulations.\n

\n

\n MUDSLIDE (I.E., MUDFLOW) PRONE AREA: An area with land surfaces and slopes of unconsolidated\n material where the history, geology, and climate indicate a potential for mudflow.\n

\n

\n NATIONAL FLOOD INSURANCE PROGRAM (NFIP): The NFIP is a Federal program created by\n Congress to mitigate future flood losses nationwide through sound, community-enforced\n building and zoning ordinances and to provide access to affordable, federally backed\n flood insurance protection for property owners.\n

\n

\n NEW CONSTRUCTION: For floodplain management purposes, a structure for which the start\n of construction commenced on or after the effective date of a floodplain management\n regulation adopted by a community and includes any subsequent improvements to such\n structures.\n

\n

\n Any construction started after September 6, 2002, and before the effective start date\n of this floodplain management ordinance is subject to the ordinance in effect at the\n time the permit was issued, provided the start of construction was within one hundred\n eighty (180) days of permit issuance.\n

\n

\n NEW MANUFACTURED HOME PARK OR SUBDIVISION: A place where the construction of facilities\n for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including\n at a minimum the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and final\n site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is completed on or after the effective\n date of floodplain management regulations adopted by a community on September 6, 2002.\n

\n

\n POST-FIRM: Construction or other development for which the start of construction occurred\n on or after the effective date of the initial Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM).\n

\n

\n PRE-FIRM: Construction or other development for which the start of construction occurred\n before September 6, 2002, the effective date of the initial Flood Insurance Rate Map\n (FIRM).\n

\n

\n RECREATIONAL VEHICLE: A vehicle that is:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Built on a single chassis; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Four hundred (400) square feet or less when measured at the largest horizontal projection;\n and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Designed to be self-propelled or permanently towed by a light duty truck; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Designed primarily not for use as a permanent dwelling but as temporary living quarters\n for recreational, camping, travel, or seasonal use.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n REGULATORY FLOODWAY: See FLOODWAY.\n

\n

\n REMEDY A VIOLATION: To bring the structure or other development into compliance with\n State or local floodplain management regulations, or, if this is not possible, to\n reduce the impacts of its non-compliance. Ways that impacts may be reduced include\n protecting the structure or other affected development from flood damages, implementing\n the enforcement provisions of this chapter or otherwise deterring future similar violations,\n or reducing Federal financial exposure with regard to the structure or other development.\n

\n

\n REPETITIVE LOSS STRUCTURE: An NFIP-insured structure that has had at least two (2)\n paid flood losses of more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) each in any ten (10)\n year period since 1978.\n

\n

\n RIVERINE: Relating to, formed by, or resembling a river (including tributaries), stream,\n brook, etc.\n

\n

\n SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD AREA (SFHA): The land in the floodplain within a community subject\n to a one percent (1%) or greater chance of flooding in any given year. For purposes\n of these regulations, the term \"special flood hazard area\" is synonymous in meaning\n with the phrase \"area of special flood hazard\".\n

\n

\n START OF CONSTRUCTION: Includes substantial improvement, and means the date the building\n permit was issued, provided the actual start of construction, repair, reconstruction,\n rehabilitation, addition placement, or other improvement was within one hundred eighty\n (180) days of the permit date. The actual start means either the first placement of\n permanent construction of a structure on a site, such as the pouring of slab or footings,\n the installation of piles, the construction of columns, or any work beyond the stage\n of excavation; or the placement of a manufactured home on a foundation. Permanent\n construction does not include land preparation, such as clearing, grading, and filling;\n nor does it include the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does it include\n excavation for a basement, footings, piers, or foundations or the erection of temporary\n forms; nor does it include the installation on the property of accessory buildings,\n such as garages or sheds not occupied as dwelling units or not part of the main structure.\n For a substantial improvement, the actual start of construction means the first alteration\n of any wall, ceiling, floor, or other structural part of a building, whether or not\n that alteration affects the external dimensions of the building.\n

\n

\n STRUCTURE: A walled and roofed building, including a gas or liquid storage tank that\n is principally above ground, as well as a manufactured home.\n

\n

\n SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE: Damage of any origin sustained by a structure whereby the cost\n of restoring the structure to its before-damaged condition would equal or exceed fifty\n percent (50%) of its market value before the damage occurred. See definition of \"substantial\n improvement\". Substantial damage also means flood-related damage sustained by a structure\n on two separate occasions during a ten (10) year period for which the cost of repairs\n at the time of each such flood event, on the average, equals or exceeds twenty-five\n percent (25%) of the market value of the structure before the damage occurred.\n

\n

\n SUBSTANTIAL IMPROVEMENT: Any reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition, or other improvement\n of a structure, the cost of which equals or exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the market\n value of the structure before the \"start of construction\" of the improvement. This\n term includes structures which have incurred \"substantial damage\", regardless of the\n actual repair work performed. The term does not, however, include either:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any project for improvement of a structure to correct existing violations of state\n or local health, sanitary, or safety code specifications which have been identified\n by the local code enforcement official and which are the minimum necessary to assure\n safe living conditions; or\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any alteration of a \"historic structure\", provided that the alteration will not preclude\n the structure's continued designation as a \"historic structure\" and the alteration\n is approved by variance issued pursuant to this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n TECHNICAL BULLETINS AND TECHNICAL FACT SHEETS: FEMA publications that provide guidance\n concerning the building performance standards of the NFIP, which are contained in\n 44 CFR § 60.3. The bulletins and fact sheets are intended for use primarily by State\n and local officials responsible for interpreting and enforcing NFIP regulations and\n by members of the development community, such as design professionals and builders.\n New bulletins, as well as updates of existing bulletins, are issued periodically as\n needed. The bulletins do not create regulations. Rather they provide specific guidance\n for complying with the minimum requirements of existing NFIP regulations. It should\n be noted that Technical Bulletins and Technical Fact Sheets provide guidance on the\n minimum requirements of the NFIP regulations. State or community requirements that\n exceed those of the NFIP take precedence. Design professionals should contact the\n community officials to determine whether more restrictive State or local regulations\n apply to the building or site in question. All applicable standards of the State or\n local building code must also be met for any building in a flood hazard area.\n

\n

\n TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED: Having the temperature regulated by a heating and/or cooling\n system, built-in or appliance.\n

\n

\n VARIANCE: A grant of relief by the governing body from a requirement of this chapter.\n

\n

\n VIOLATION: The failure of a structure or other development to be fully compliant with\n the community's floodplain management regulations. A structure or other development\n without the finished construction elevation certificate, other certifications, or\n other evidence of compliance required in 44 CFR § 60.3(b)(5), (c)(4), (c)(10), (d)(3),\n (e)(2), (e) (4), or (e)(5) is presumed to be in violation until such time as that\n documentation is provided.\n

\n

\n WATER SURFACE ELEVATION: The height, in relation to the National Geodetic Vertical\n Datum (NGVD) of 1929 or the North American Vertical Datum (NAVD) of 1988 (or other\n specified datum), of floods of various magnitudes and frequencies in the floodplains\n of coastal or riverine areas.\n

\n

\n WATERCOURSE: A lake, river, creek, stream, wash, channel, or other topographic feature\n on or over which waters flow at least periodically. Watercourse includes specifically\n designated areas in which substantial flood damage may occur.\n

\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":false,"CompareStatus":4,"DocOrderId":662,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT10FLCO","NodeDepth":3,"TitleHtml":"
10-1-3: - General Provisions
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-3GEPR","Title":"10-1-3: - General Provisions","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Lands to Which This Chapter Applies: This chapter shall apply to all special flood\n hazard areas within the jurisdiction of the City of Star. Nothing in this chapter\n is intended to allow uses or structures that are otherwise prohibited by the zoning\n ordinance.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Basis for Special Flood Hazard Areas: The City of Star, Idaho lies within two counties:\n 1) Ada County and 2) Canyon County. The special flood hazard areas identified by the\n Federal Insurance Administrator in a scientific and engineering report for the portion\n of the City that lies within Canyon County titled \"Flood Insurance Study (FIS) for\n Canyon County, Idaho and incorporated Areas\", dated June 7, 2019, and the portion\n of the City that lies within Ada County titled \"The Flood Insurance Study for Ada\n County, Idaho and Incorporated Areas\" dated June 19, 2020, and accompanying Flood\n Insurance Rate Maps (FIRM) or Digital Flood Insurance Rate Maps (DFIRM), and other\n supporting data, are adopted by reference and declared a part of this chapter. The\n FIS and the FIRM are on file at the office of the Star City Clerk, 10769 W. State\n Street, Star, Idaho.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Establishment of Floodplain Development Permit: A floodplain development permit shall\n be required in conformance with the provisions of this chapter prior to the commencement\n of any development activities within special flood hazard areas determined in accordance\n with the provisions of subsection B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Compliance: No structure or land shall hereafter be located, extended, converted,\n altered, or developed in any way without full compliance with the terms of this chapter\n and other applicable regulations.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Abrogation and Greater Restrictions: This chapter shall not in any way repeal, abrogate,\n impair, or remove the necessity of compliance with any other laws, ordinances, regulations,\n easements, covenants, or deed restrictions, etc. However, where this chapter and another\n conflict or overlap, whichever imposes more stringent or greater restrictions shall\n control.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n F.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Interpretation: In the interpretation and application of this chapter all provisions\n shall be:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Considered as minimum requirements;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Liberally construed in favor of the governing body; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Deemed neither to limit nor repeal any other powers granted under state statutes.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n G.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Warning and Disclaimer of Liability: The degree of flood protection required by this\n chapter is considered reasonable for regulatory purposes and is based on scientific\n and engineering considerations. Larger floods can and will occur. Flood heights may\n be increased by man-made or natural causes. This chapter does not imply that land\n outside the special flood hazard areas or uses permitted within such areas will be\n free from flooding or flood damages. This chapter shall not create liability on the\n part of the City of Star or by any officer or employee thereof for flood damages that\n result from reliance on this chapter or an administrative decision lawfully made hereunder.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n H.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Penalties for Violation:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No structure or land shall hereafter be located, extended, converted, or altered unless\n in full compliance with the terms of this chapter and other applicable regulations.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Violation of the provisions of this chapter or failure to comply with any of its requirements,\n including violation of conditions and safeguards established in connection with grants\n of variance or special exceptions, shall constitute a misdemeanor. Any person who\n violates this chapter or fails to comply with any of its requirements shall, upon\n conviction thereof, be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00) or imprisoned\n for not more than one hundred eighty (180) days, or both. Each day the violation continues\n shall be considered a separate offense. Nothing herein contained shall prevent the\n City of Star from taking such other lawful actions as is necessary to prevent or remedy\n any violation.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Illegal placement of fill, debris or other waste material within a SFHA is a violation\n of the provisions of this chapter and therefore is subject to the provisions of subsection\n H2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021)\n
