10-1-4: - Administration
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-4AD","Title":"10-1-4: - Administration","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Designation of Floodplain Ordinance Administrator: The Mayor or their designee, hereinafter\n referred to as the \"Floodplain Administrator\", is hereby appointed to administer and\n implement the provisions of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Duties and Responsibilities of the Floodplain Administrator: The Floodplain Administrator\n shall perform, but not be limited to, the following duties:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Review all floodplain development applications and issue permits for all proposed\n development within special flood hazard areas to assure that the requirements of this\n chapter have been satisfied.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Review all proposed development within special flood hazard areas to assure that all\n necessary local, State, and Federal permits have been received, including section\n 404 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act Amendments of 1972, 33 USC § 1334.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Notify adjacent communities and the Idaho Department of Water Resources State Coordinator\n for the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) prior to any alteration or relocation\n of a watercourse and submit evidence of such notification to the Federal Insurance\n Administrator (FIA). (This is the LOMC procedure.)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Assure that the flood carrying capacity within the altered or relocated portion of\n any watercourse is maintained. (This is a hydraulic and hydrology analysis.)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Prevent encroachments into floodways unless the certification and flood hazard reduction\n provisions of section 10-1-5E are met.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Obtain and maintain actual elevation (in relation to mean sea level) of the lowest\n floor (including basement) and all attendant utilities of all new and substantially\n improved structures, in accordance with the provisions of subsection C3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Obtain and maintain actual elevation (in relation to mean sea level) to which all\n new and substantially improved structures and utilities have been floodproofed, in\n accordance with the provisions of subsection C3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Review plans to verify public utilities are constructed in accordance with the provisions\n of section 10-1-5, subsection A5 through A7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When floodproofing is utilized for a particular structure, obtain and maintain certifications\n from a registered professional engineer or architect in accordance with the provisions\n of subsection C3 and section 10-1-5B2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 10.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Where interpretation is needed as to the exact location of boundaries of the special\n flood hazard areas, and floodways (for example, where there appears to be a conflict\n between a mapped boundary and actual field conditions), make the necessary interpretation.\n The person contesting the location of the boundary shall be given a reasonable opportunity\n to appeal the interpretation as provided in this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 11.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When base flood elevation (BFE) data has not been provided in accordance with the\n provisions of section 10-1-3B, obtain, review, and reasonably utilize any BFE data,\n along with floodway data available from a Federal, State, or other source, including\n data developed pursuant to section 10-1-5C2, in order to administer the provisions\n of this ordinance.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 12.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When base flood elevation (BFE) data is provided but no floodway data has been provided\n in accordance with the provisions of section 10-1-3B require that no new construction,\n substantial improvements, or other development (including fill) shall be permitted\n within Zones A1-30 and AE on the community's FIRM, unless it is demonstrated that\n the cumulative effect of the proposed development, when combined with all other existing\n and anticipated development, will not increase the water surface elevation of the\n base flood more than one foot at any point within the community. (This is a hydraulic\n and hydrology analysis.)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 13.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When the lowest floor and the lowest adjacent grade of a structure or the lowest ground\n elevation of a parcel in a special flood hazard area (SFHA) is above the base flood\n elevation (BFE), advise the property owner of the option to apply for a Letter of\n Map Amendment (LOMA) from FEMA. Maintain a copy of the LOMA issued by FEMA in the\n floodplain development permit file.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 14.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Permanently maintain all records that pertain to the administration of this chapter\n and make these records available for public inspection, recognizing that such information\n may be subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 15.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Make on-site inspections of work in progress. As the work pursuant to a floodplain\n development permit progresses, the Floodplain Administrator shall make as many inspections\n of the work as may be necessary to ensure that the work is being done according to\n the provisions of the local ordinance and the terms of the permit. In exercising this\n power, the Floodplain Administrator has a right, upon presentation of proper credentials,\n to enter on any premises within the jurisdiction of the Community at any reasonable\n hour for the purposes of inspection or other enforcement action.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 16.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Issue stop-work orders as required. Whenever a building or part thereof is being constructed,\n reconstructed, altered, or repaired in violation of this chapter, the Floodplain Administrator\n may order the work to be immediately stopped. The stop-work order shall be in writing\n and directed to the person doing or in charge of the work. The stop-work order shall\n state the specific work to be stopped, the specific reason(s) for the stoppage, and\n the condition(s) under which the work may be resumed. Violation of a stop-work order\n constitutes a misdemeanor.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 17.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Revoke floodplain development permits as required. The Floodplain Administrator may\n revoke and require the return of the floodplain development permit by notifying the\n permit holder in writing stating the reason(s) for the revocation. Permits shall be\n revoked for any substantial departure from the approved application, plans, and specifications;\n for refusal or failure to comply with the requirements of State or local laws; or\n for false statements or misrepresentations made in securing the permit. Any floodplain\n development permit mistakenly issued in violation of an applicable State or local\n law may also be revoked.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 18.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Make periodic inspections throughout the special flood hazard areas within the jurisdiction\n of the community. The Floodplain Administrator and each member of his or her inspections\n department shall have a right, upon presentation of proper credentials, to enter on\n any premises within the territorial jurisdiction of the department at any reasonable\n hour for the purposes of inspection or other enforcement action.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 19.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Follow through with corrective procedures of subsection D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 20.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Review, provide input, and make recommendations for variance requests.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 21.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Maintain a current map repository to include, but not limited to, the FIS Report,\n FIRM and other official flood maps, and studies adopted in accordance with the provisions\n of subsection 10-1-3B of this chapter, including any revisions thereto including Letters\n of Map Change, issued by FEMA. Notify the NFIP State Coordinator and FEMA of your\n community's mapping needs.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 22.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Coordinate revisions to FIS reports and FIRMs, including Letters of Map Revision Based\n on Fill (LOMR-Fs) and Letters of Map Revision (LOMRs).\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 23.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A community's base flood elevations may increase or decrease resulting from physical\n changes affecting flooding conditions. As soon as practicable, but not later than\n six (6) months after the date such information becomes available, a community shall\n notify the Federal Insurance Administrator (FIA) of the changes by submitting technical\n or scientific data in accordance with this part. Such a submission is necessary so\n that upon confirmation of those physical changes affecting flooding conditions, risk\n premium rates and floodplain management requirements will be based upon current data.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 24.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Upon occurrence, notify the Federal Insurance Administrator (FIA) in writing whenever\n the boundaries of the community have been modified by annexation or the community\n has otherwise assumed or no longer has authority to adopt and enforce flood plain\n management regulations for a particular area. In order that all FHBM's and FIRM's\n accurately represent the community's boundaries, include within such notification\n a copy of a map of the community suitable for reproduction, clearly delineating the\n new corporate limits or new area for which the community has assumed or relinquished\n floodplain management regulatory authority.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Floodplain Development Application, Permit, and Certification Requirements:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Application Requirements: Application for a floodplain development permit shall be\n made to the Floodplain Administrator prior to any development activities located within\n special flood hazard areas. The following items shall be presented to the Floodplain\n Administrator to apply for a floodplain development permit:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A plot plan drawn to scale which shall include, but shall not be limited to, the following\n specific details of the proposed floodplain development:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The nature, location, dimensions, and elevations of the area of development/disturbance;\n existing and proposed structures, utility systems, grading/pavement areas, fill materials,\n storage areas, drainage facilities, and other development;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The boundary of the special flood hazard area as delineated on the FIRM or other flood\n map as determined in subsection 10-1-3B, or a statement that the entire lot is within\n the special flood hazard area;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The flood zone(s) designation of the proposed development area as determined on the\n FIRM or other flood map as determined in subsection 10-1-3B;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (4)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The boundary of the floodway(s) as determined in subsection 10-1-3B;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (5)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The base flood elevation (BFE) where provided as set forth in subsections 10-1-3B.\n 10-1-3C, or 10-1-5C;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (6)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The old and new location of any watercourse that will be altered or relocated as a\n result of proposed development; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (7)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The certification of the plot plan by a registered land surveyor or professional engineer.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Proposed elevation, and method thereof, of all development within a special flood\n hazard area including but not limited to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Elevation in relation to mean sea level of the proposed lowest floor (including basement)\n of all structures;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Elevation in relation to mean sea level to which any non- residential structure in\n Zone A, AE, AH, AO, or A1-30 will be floodproofed; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Elevation in relation to mean sea level to which any proposed utility equipment and\n machinery will be elevated or floodproofed.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If floodproofing, a Floodproofing Certificate (FEMA Form 086-0-33) with supporting\n data, an operational plan, and an inspection and maintenance plan that include, but\n are not limited to, installation, exercise, and maintenance of floodproofing measures\n will be required prior to certificate of occupancy/completion.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A foundation plan, drawn to scale, which shall include details of the proposed foundation\n system to ensure all provisions of this chapter are met. These details include but\n are not limited to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The proposed method of elevation, if applicable (i.e., fill, solid foundation perimeter\n wall, solid backfilled foundation, open foundation, or on columns/posts/piers/piles/shear\n walls); and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Openings to facilitate automatic equalization of hydrostatic flood forces on walls\n in accordance with subsection 10-1-5A8b when solid foundation perimeter walls are\n used in Zones A, AE, AH, AO, and A1-30.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Usage details of any enclosed areas below the lowest floor.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Plans and/or details for the protection of public utilities and facilities such as\n sewer, gas, electrical, and water systems to be located and constructed to minimize\n flood damage.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n g.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Certification that all other local, State, and Federal permits required prior to floodplain\n development permit issuance have been received.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n h.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Documentation for placement of recreational vehicles and/or temporary structures,\n when applicable, to ensure that the provisions of subsections 10-1-5B5 and 10-1-5B6\n of this chapter are met.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n i.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A description of proposed watercourse alteration or relocation, when applicable, including\n an engineering report on the effects of the proposed project on the flood-carrying\n capacity of the watercourse and the effects to properties located both upstream and\n downstream; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A map (if not shown on plot plan) showing the location of the proposed watercourse\n alteration or relocation. (This is a Hydraulic & Hydrology Analysis, & may involve\n the LOMC procedure.)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Permit Requirements: The floodplain development permit shall include, but not be limited\n to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A complete description of all the development to be permitted under the floodplain\n development permit (i.e., house, garage, pool, septic, bulkhead, cabana, pole barn,\n chicken coop, pier, bridge, mining, dredging, filling, rip-rap, docks, grading, paving,\n excavation or drilling operations, or storage of equipment or materials, etc.).\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The special flood hazard area determination for the proposed development in accordance\n with available data specified in subsection 10-1-3B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The flood protection elevation required for the lowest floor and all attendant utilities.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The flood protection elevation required for the protection of all utility equipment\n and machinery.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All certification submittal requirements with timelines.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A statement that no fill material or other development shall encroach into the floodway\n of any watercourse, as applicable.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n g.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The flood openings requirements.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n h.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All floodplain development permits shall be conditional upon the start of construction\n of work within one hundred eighty (180) days. A floodplain development permit shall\n expire one hundred eighty (180) days after issuance unless the permitted activity\n has commenced as per the start of construction definition.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n i.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Fully enclosed areas below the lowest floor are usable solely for parking of vehicles,\n building access, or storage.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n j.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All materials below BFE/FPE must be flood-resistant materials.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Certification Requirements:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Elevation Certificates:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A Construction Drawings Elevation Certificate (FEMA Form 86-0-33) is required prior\n to the actual start of any new construction. It shall be the duty of the permit holder\n to submit to the Floodplain Administrator a certification of the elevation of the\n lowest floor, in relation to mean sea level. The Floodplain Administrator shall review\n the certificate data submitted. Deficiencies detected by such review shall be corrected\n by the permit holder prior to the beginning of construction. Failure to submit the\n certification or failure to make required corrections shall be cause to deny a floodplain\n development permit.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A final as-built Finished Construction Elevation Certificate (FEMA Form 86-0-33) is\n required after construction is completed and prior to Certificate of Compliance/Occupancy\n issuance. It shall be the duty of the permit holder to submit to the Floodplain Administrator\n a certification of final as-built construction of the elevation of the lowest floor\n and all attendant utilities. The Floodplain Administrator shall review the certificate\n data submitted. Deficiencies detected by such review shall be corrected by the permit\n holder immediately and prior to Certificate of Compliance/Occupancy issuance. In some\n instances, another certification may be required to certify corrected as-built construction.\n Failure to submit the certification or failure to make required corrections shall\n be cause to withhold the issuance of a Certificate of Compliance/Occupancy.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Finished Construction Elevation Certificate certifier shall provide at least two\n (2) photographs showing the front and rear of the building taken within ninety (90)\n days from the date of certification. The photographs must be taken with views confirming\n the building description and diagram number provided in subsection A. To the extent\n possible, these photographs should show the entire building including foundation.\n If the building has split-level or multi-level areas, provide at least two (2) additional\n photographs showing side views of the building. In addition, when applicable, provide\n a photograph of the foundation showing a representative example of the flood openings\n or vents. All photographs must be in color and measure at least three inches by three\n inches (3\" × 3\"). Digital photographs are acceptable.\n

\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Floodproofing Certificate: If non-residential floodproofing is used to meet the flood\n protection elevation requirements, design plans, with supporting data, an operational\n plan, and an inspection and maintenance plan are required prior to the actual start\n of any new construction. It shall be the duty of the permit holder to submit to the\n Floodplain Administrator a certification of the floodproofed design elevation of the\n lowest floor and all attendant utilities, in relation to mean sea level. Floodproofing\n certification shall be prepared by or under the direct supervision of a professional\n engineer or architect and certified by same. The Floodplain Administrator shall review\n the certificate data, the operational plan, and the inspection and maintenance plan.\n Deficiencies detected by such review shall be corrected by the applicant prior to\n permit approval. Failure to submit the certification or failure to make required corrections\n shall be cause to deny a floodplain development permit. Prior to request for a Certificate\n of Compliance/Occupancy a Floodproofing Certificate (FEMA Form 086-0-34) shall be\n provided to the Floodplain Administrator for review and approval.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If a manufactured home is placed within Zone A, AE, AH, AO, or A1-30 and the elevation\n of the chassis is more than thirty-six inches (36\") in height above grade, an engineered\n foundation certification is required in accordance with the provisions of subsection\n 10-1-5B3b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If a watercourse is to be altered or relocated, the following shall all be submitted\n by the permit applicant prior to issuance of a floodplain development permit:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A description of the extent of watercourse alteration or relocation; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A professional engineer's certified report on the effects of the proposed project\n on the flood-carrying capacity of the watercourse and the effects to properties located\n both upstream and downstream; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A map showing the location of the proposed watercourse alteration or relocation; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (4)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An Idaho Stream Channel Alteration Permit approval shall be provided by the applicant\n to the Floodplain Administrator.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Certification Exemptions: The following structures are exempt from the elevation/floodproofing\n certification requirements specified in subsections C3a and C3b of this section:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Recreational vehicles meeting requirements of subsection 10-1-5B5a;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Temporary structures meeting requirements of subsection 10-1-5B6; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures less than two hundred (200) square feet meeting requirements\n of subsection 10-1-5B7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Determinations for Existing Buildings and Structures: For applications for building\n permits to improve buildings and structures, including alterations, movement, enlargement,\n replacement, repair, change of occupancy, additions, rehabilitations, renovations,\n improvements, repairs of damage, and any other improvement of or work on such buildings\n and structures, the Floodplain Administrator, in coordination with the Building Official,\n shall:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Estimate the market value or require the applicant to obtain an appraisal of the market\n value prepared by a qualified independent appraiser, of the building or structure\n before the start of construction of the proposed work. In the case of repair, the\n market value of the building or structure shall be the market value before the damage\n occurred and before any repairs are made;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Compare the cost to perform the improvement, the cost to repair a damaged building\n to its pre-damaged condition, or the combined costs of improvements and repairs, if\n applicable, to the market value of the building or structure;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Determine and document whether the proposed work constitutes substantial improvement\n or repair of substantial damage; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Notify the applicant if it is determined that the work constitutes substantial improvement\n or repair of substantial damage and that compliance with the flood resistant construction\n requirements of the adopted Idaho Building Code and this chapter is required.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Corrective Procedures:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Violations to Be Corrected: When the Floodplain Administrator finds Violations of\n applicable State and local laws, it shall be his or her duty to notify the owner or\n occupant of the building of the violation. The owner or occupant shall immediately\n remedy each of the violations of law cited in such notification.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Actions in Event of Failure to Take Corrective Action: If the owner of a building\n or property shall fail to take prompt corrective action, the Floodplain Administrator\n shall give the owner written notice, by certified or registered mail to the owner's\n last known address or by personal service, stating:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That the building or property is in violation of the floodplain management regulations;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That a hearing will be held before the Floodplain Administrator at a designated place\n and time, not later than ten (10) days after the date of the notice, at which time\n the owner shall be entitled to be heard in person or by counsel and to present arguments\n and evidence pertaining to the matter; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That following the hearing, the Floodplain Administrator may issue an order to alter,\n vacate, or demolish the building; or to remove fill as applicable.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Order to Take Corrective Action: If, upon a hearing held pursuant to the notice prescribed\n above, the Floodplain Administrator shall find that the building or development is\n in violation of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance, he or she shall issue an order\n in writing to the owner, requiring the owner to remedy the violation within a specified\n time period, not less than sixty (60) calendar days, nor more than one hundred and\n eighty (180) calendar days. Where the Floodplain Administrator finds that there is\n imminent danger to life or other property, he or she may order that corrective action\n be taken in such lesser period as may be feasible.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Appeal: Any owner who has received an order to take corrective action may appeal the\n order to the local elected governing body by giving notice of appeal in writing to\n the Floodplain Administrator and the clerk within ten (10) days following issuance\n of the final order. In the absence of an appeal, the order of the Floodplain Administrator\n shall be final. The local governing body shall hear an appeal within a reasonable\n time and may affirm, modify and affirm, or revoke the order.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Failure to Comply with Order: If the owner of a building or property fails to comply\n with an order to take corrective action for which no appeal has been made or fails\n to comply with an order of the governing body following an appeal, the owner shall\n be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished at the discretion of the court.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variance Procedures:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The City Council, hereinafter referred to as the \"appeal board\", shall hear and decide\n requests for variances from the requirements of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances may be issued for:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The repair or rehabilitation of historic structures upon the determination that the\n proposed repair or rehabilitation will not preclude the structure's continued designation\n as a historic structure and that the variance is the minimum necessary to preserve\n the historic character and design of the structure;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Functionally dependent facilities, if determined to meet the definition as stated\n in section 10-1-2, provided provisions of subsections E8b, E8c, and E8d have been\n satisfied, and such facilities are protected by methods that minimize flood damages\n during the base flood and create no additional threats to public safety; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any other type of development, provided it meets the requirements of this section.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In passing upon variances, the appeal board shall consider all technical evaluations,\n all relevant factors, all standards specified in other sections of this chapter, and:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The danger that materials may be swept onto other lands to the injury of others;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The danger to life and property due to flooding or erosion damage;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The susceptibility of the proposed facility and its contents to flood damage and the\n effect of such damage on the individual owner;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The importance of the services provided by the proposed facility to the community;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The necessity to the facility of a waterfront location as defined under section 10-1-2\n as a functionally dependent facility, where applicable;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The availability of alternative locations, not subject to flooding or erosion damage,\n for the proposed use;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n g.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The compatibility of the proposed use with existing and anticipated development;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n h.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The relationship of the proposed use to the comprehensive plan and floodplain management\n program for that area;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n i.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The safety of access to the property in times of flood for ordinary and emergency\n vehicles;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n j.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The expected heights, velocity, duration, rate of rise, and sediment transport of\n the floodwaters and the effects of wave action, if applicable, expected at the site;\n and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n k.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The costs of providing governmental services during and after flood conditions including\n maintenance and repair of public utilities and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical\n and water systems, and streets and bridges.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n l.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances as interpreted in the national flood insurance program are based on the\n general zoning law principle that they pertain to a physical piece of property; variances\n are not personal in nature and do not pertain to the structure, its inhabitants, economic\n or financial circumstances. Variances primarily address small lots in densely populated\n residential neighborhoods. As such, variances from the flood elevations should be\n quite rare. The applicant shall carefully review FEMA's Floodplain Management Bulletin\n entitled \"Variances and the National Flood Insurance Program\" (FEMA P-993 / July 2014).\n This document is available from City Staff.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The applicant shall include a written report addressing each of the above factors\n in subsections E3a through E3k with their application for a variance.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Upon consideration of the factors listed above and the purposes of this chapter, the\n appeal board may attach such conditions to the granting of variances as it deems necessary\n to further the purposes and objectives of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any applicant to whom a variance is granted shall be given written notice specifying\n the difference between the base flood elevation (BFE) and the elevation to which the\n structure is to be built and that such construction below the BFE increases risks\n to life and property, and that the issuance of a variance to construct a structure\n below the BFE will result in increased premium rates for flood insurance up to twenty-five\n dollars ($25.00) per one hundred dollars ($100.00) of insurance coverage. Such notification\n shall be maintained with a record of all variance actions, including justification\n for their issuance.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Floodplain Administrator shall maintain the records of all appeal actions and\n report any variances to the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the State of Idaho\n upon request.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Conditions for Variances:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances shall not be issued when the variance will make the structure in violation\n of other Federal, State, or local laws, regulations, or ordinances.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances shall not be issued within any designated floodway if the variance would\n result in any increase in flood levels during the base flood discharge.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances shall only be issued upon a determination that the variance is the minimum\n necessary, considering the flood hazard, to afford relief.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances shall only be issued prior to development permit approval.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Variances shall only be issued upon:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A showing of good and sufficient cause;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A determination that failure to grant the variance would result in exceptional hardship;\n and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A determination that the granting of a variance will not result in increased flood\n heights, additional threats to public safety, or extraordinary public expense, create\n nuisance, cause fraud on or victimization of the public, or conflict with existing\n local laws or ordinances.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A variance may be issued for solid waste disposal facilities or sites, hazardous waste\n management facilities, salvage yards, and chemical storage facilities that are located\n in special flood hazard areas provided that all of the following conditions are met:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The use serves a critical need in the community.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No feasible location exists for the use outside the special flood hazard area.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The lowest floor of any structure is elevated or floodproofed to at least the flood\n protection elevation.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The use complies with all other applicable Federal, State and local laws.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 10.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The City of Star will notify the State NFIP Coordinator of the Idaho Department of\n Water Resources of its intention to grant a variance at least thirty (30) calendar\n days prior to granting the variance.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 11.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any person aggrieved by the decision of the appeal board may appeal such decision\n to the Court, as provided in Idaho Code section 67-6535.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021; Ord. No. 413-2025 § 1, 2-18-2025)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":false,"CompareStatus":4,"DocOrderId":664,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT10FLCO","NodeDepth":3,"TitleHtml":"
10-1-5: - Provisions for Flood Hazard Reduction
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-5PRFLHARE","Title":"10-1-5: - Provisions for Flood Hazard Reduction","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n General Standards: In all special flood hazard areas the following provisions are\n required:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new construction, substantial improvements, and development shall be designed\n (or modified) and adequately anchored to prevent flotation, collapse, and lateral\n movement of the structure resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, including\n the effects of buoyancy.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new construction, substantial improvements, and development shall be constructed\n with materials and utility equipment resistant to flood damage in accordance with\n the Technical Bulletin 2, Flood Damage-Resistant Materials Requirements, and available\n from the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new construction, substantial improvements, and development shall be constructed\n by methods and practices that minimize flood damages.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new and replacement electrical, heating, ventilation, plumbing, air conditioning\n equipment, and other service facilities shall be designed and/or located so as to\n prevent water from entering or accumulating within the components during conditions\n of flooding to the Flood Protection Elevation. These include, but are not limited\n to, HVAC equipment, water softener units, bath/kitchen fixtures, ductwork, electric/gas\n meter panels/boxes, utility/cable boxes, hot water heaters, and electric outlets/switches.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate\n infiltration of floodwaters into the system.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All new and replacement sanitary sewage systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate\n infiltration of floodwaters into the systems and discharges from the systems into\n floodwaters.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n On-site waste disposal systems shall be located and constructed to avoid impairment\n to them or contamination from them during flooding.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A fully enclosed area, of new construction and substantially improved structures,\n which is below the lowest floor and used solely for parking, access, and storage shall:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Be constructed entirely of flood resistant materials at least to the flood protection\n elevation; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Include, in Zones A, AE, AH, AO, and A1-30, flood openings to automatically equalize\n hydrostatic flood forces on walls by allowing for the entry and exit of floodwaters.\n To meet this requirement, the openings must either be certified by a professional\n engineer or architect or meet or exceed the following minimum design criteria:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A minimum of two (2) flood openings on different sides of each enclosed area subject\n to flooding;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The total net area of all flood openings must be at least one (1) square inch for\n each square foot of enclosed area subject to flooding;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (3)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If a building has more than one enclosed area, each enclosed area must have flood\n openings to allow floodwaters to automatically enter and exit;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (4)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The bottom of all required flood openings shall be no higher than BFE above the interior\n or exterior adjacent grade;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (5)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Flood openings may be equipped with screens, louvers, or other coverings or devices,\n provided they permit the automatic flow of floodwaters in both directions; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (6)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Enclosures made of flexible skirting are not considered enclosures for regulatory\n purposes, and, therefore, do not require flood openings. Masonry or flood resistant\n wood underpinning, regardless of structural status, is considered an enclosure and\n requires flood openings as outlined above.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any alteration, repair, reconstruction, or improvements to a structure, which is in\n compliance with the provisions of this chapter, shall meet the requirements of \"new\n construction\" as contained in this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 10.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Nothing in this chapter shall prevent the repair, reconstruction, or replacement of\n a building or structure existing on the effective date of this chapter and located\n totally or partially within the floodway, or stream setback, provided there is no\n additional encroachment below the flood protection elevation in the floodway, or stream\n setback, and provided that such repair, reconstruction, or replacement meets all of\n the other requirements of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 11.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n New solid waste disposal facilities and sites, hazardous waste management facilities,\n salvage yards, and chemical storage facilities shall not be permitted, except by variance\n as specified in subsection 10- 1-4E9. A structure or tank for chemical or fuel storage\n incidental to an allowed use or to the operation of a water treatment plant or wastewater\n treatment facility may be located in a special flood hazard area only if the structure\n or tank is either elevated or floodproofed to at least the flood protection elevation\n and certified in accordance with the provisions of subsection 10-1-4C3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 12.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All subdivision proposals and other development proposals shall be consistent with\n the need to minimize flood damage and determined to be reasonably safe from flooding.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 13.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All subdivision proposals and other development proposals shall have public utilities\n and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical, and water systems located and constructed\n to minimize flood damage.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 14.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All subdivision proposals and other development proposals shall have adequate drainage\n provided to reduce exposure to flood hazards.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 15.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All subdivision proposals and other development proposals shall have received all\n necessary permits from those governmental agencies for which approval is required\n by Federal or State law, including Section 404 of the Federal Water Pollution Control\n Act Amendments of 1972, 33 USC § 1334.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 16.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All subdivision proposals and other development proposals greater than fifty (50)\n lots or five (5) acres, whichever is the lesser, shall include within such proposals\n base flood elevation data.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 17.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When a structure is partially located in a special flood hazard area, the entire structure\n shall meet the requirements for new construction and substantial improvements.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 18.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When a structure is located in multiple flood hazard zones or in a flood hazard risk\n zone with multiple base flood elevations, the provisions for the more restrictive\n flood hazard risk zone and the highest base flood elevation (BFE) shall apply.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 19.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Fill is prohibited in the floodway, including construction of buildings on fill. This\n includes not signing the Community Acknowledgment page for Conditional Letters or\n Letters of Map Revision (CLOMR-F or LOMR-F).\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Specific Standards: In all special flood hazard areas where base flood elevation (BFE)\n data has been provided, as set forth in subsections D or 10-2-3B, the following provisions,\n in addition to the provisions of subsection A, are required:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Residential Construction: New construction, substantial improvements, and development\n of any residential structure (including manufactured homes) shall have the lowest\n floor, including basement, elevated no lower than the flood protection elevation,\n as defined in section 10-1-2 of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Non-Residential Construction: New construction, substantial improvements, and development\n of any commercial, industrial, or other non-residential structure shall have the lowest\n floor, including basement, elevated no lower than the flood protection elevation,\n as defined in section 10-1-2 of this chapter. Structures located in Zones A, AE, AH,\n AO, and A1-30 may be floodproofed to the flood protection elevation in lieu of elevation\n provided that all areas of the structure, together with attendant utility and sanitary\n facilities, below the flood protection elevation are watertight with walls substantially\n impermeable to the passage of water, using structural components having the capability\n of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and the effect of buoyancy. For AH\n and AO Zones, the floodproofing elevation shall be in accordance with subsection F2.\n A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the floodproofing\n standards of this subsection are satisfied. Such certification shall be provided to\n the Floodplain Administrator as set forth in subsection 10-1-4C3, along with the operational\n plan and the inspection and maintenance plan.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Manufactured Homes:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n New and replacement manufactured homes shall be elevated so that the lowest floor\n of the manufactured home is no lower than the flood protection elevation, as defined\n in section 10-1-2 of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Manufactured homes shall be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation\n to resist flotation, collapse, and lateral movement, either by certified engineered\n foundation system, or in accordance with the most current edition of the Idaho Division\n of Building Safety's \"Idaho Manufactured Home Installation Standard\" in accordance\n with Idaho Code section 44-2201(2). Additionally, when the elevation would be met\n by an elevation of the chassis thirty-six inches (36\") or less above the grade at\n the site, the chassis shall be supported by reinforced piers or engineered foundation.\n When the elevation of the chassis is above thirty-six inches (36\") in height, an engineering\n certification is required.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All enclosures or skirting below the lowest floor shall meet the requirements of subsections\n A8a and A8b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An evacuation plan must be developed for evacuation of all residents of all new, substantially\n improved, or substantially damaged manufactured home parks or subdivisions located\n within flood prone areas. This plan shall be filed with and approved by the Floodplain\n Administrator and the local Emergency Management Coordinator.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additions/Improvements:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additions and/or improvements to pre-FIRM structures when the addition and/or improvements\n in combination with any interior modifications to the existing structure are:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Not a substantial improvement, the addition and/or improvements must be designed to\n minimize flood damages and must not be any more non-conforming than the existing structure;\n or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A substantial improvement, both the existing structure and the addition and/or improvements\n must comply with the standards for new construction.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additions to non-compliant post-FIRM structures that are a substantial improvement\n with no modifications to the existing structure other than a standard door in the\n common wall shall require only the addition to comply with the standards for new construction.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additions and/or improvements to non-compliant post-FIRM structures when the addition\n and/or improvements in combination with any interior modifications to the existing\n structure are:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Not a substantial improvement, the addition and/or improvements only must comply with\n the standards for new construction; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A substantial improvement, both the existing structure and the addition and/or improvements\n must comply with the standards for new construction.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Recreational Vehicles: Recreational vehicles shall be either:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Temporary Placement:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Be on-site for fewer than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days or be fully licensed\n and ready for highway use (a recreational vehicle is ready for highway use if it is\n on its wheels or jacking system, is attached to the site only by quick disconnect\n type utilities, and has no permanently attached additions); or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Permanent Placement:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Recreational vehicles that do not meet the limitations of temporary placement shall\n meet all the requirements for new construction, as set forth in subsection A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Temporary Non-Residential Structures: Prior to the issuance of a floodplain development\n permit for a temporary structure, the applicant must submit to the Floodplain Administrator\n a plan for the removal of such structure(s) in the event of a flash flood or other\n type of flood warning notification. The following information shall be submitted in\n writing to the Floodplain Administrator for review and written approval:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A specified time period for which the temporary use will be permitted. Time specified\n may not exceed six (6) months, renewable up to one (1) year;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The name, address, and phone number of the individual responsible for the removal\n of the temporary structure;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The time frame prior to the event at which a structure will be removed (i.e., immediately\n upon flood warning notification);\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A copy of the contract or other suitable instrument with the entity responsible for\n physical removal of the structure;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Designation, accompanied by documentation, of a location outside the special flood\n hazard area, to which the temporary structure will be moved; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Temporary structures in the floodway must provide a hydraulic and hydrology analysis\n along with a no-rise certification.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory Structures (Appurtenant Structures): When accessory structures (sheds, detached\n garages, etc.) used solely for parking, and storage are to be placed within a special\n flood hazard area, elevation or floodproofing certifications are required for all\n accessory structures in accordance with subsection 10-1-4C3, and the following criteria\n shall be met:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures shall not be used for human habitation (including working, sleeping,\n living, cooking, or restroom areas);\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures shall not be temperature-controlled;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures shall be designed to have low flood damage potential;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures shall be constructed and placed on the building site so as to\n offer the minimum resistance to the flow of floodwaters;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures shall be firmly anchored in accordance with the provisions of\n subsection A1;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All utility equipment and machinery, such as electrical, shall be installed in accordance\n with the provisions of subsection A4; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n g.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Flood openings to facilitate automatic equalization of hydrostatic flood forces shall\n be provided below flood protection elevation in conformance with the provisions of\n subsection A8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n h.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory structures not used solely for parking, access, and storage must be elevated\n per subsections B1 and B2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An accessory structure with a footprint less than 200 square feet and is a minimal\n investment of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500.00) or less and satisfies\n the criteria outlined in subsections B7a through B7g above is not required to provide\n the elevation certificate per subsection B2.\n

\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Tanks: When gas and liquid storage tanks are to be placed within a special flood hazard\n area, the following criteria shall be met:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Underground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse,\n or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions\n of the base flood, including the effects of buoyancy (assuming the tank is empty);\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Elevated above-ground tanks, in flood hazard areas shall be attached to, and elevated\n to or above the design flood elevation on a supporting structure that is designed\n to prevent flotation, collapse, or lateral movement during conditions of the base\n flood. Tank-supporting structures shall meet the foundation requirements of the applicable\n flood hazard area;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Not elevated above-ground tanks may be permitted in flood hazard areas provided the\n tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse\n or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions\n of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty\n and the effects of flood-borne debris.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Tank inlets, fill openings, outlets and vents shall be:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n At or above the flood protection elevation or fitted with covers designed to prevent\n the inflow of floodwater or outflow of the contents of the tanks during conditions\n of the base flood; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Anchored to prevent lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads,\n including the effects of buoyancy, during conditions of the base flood.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Construction of Below-Grade Crawlspace:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The interior grade of a crawlspace must not be below the BFE and must not be more\n than two feet (2') below the exterior lowest adjacent grade (LAG).\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The height of the below-grade crawlspace, measured from the interior grade of the\n crawlspace to the top of the crawlspace foundation wall, must not exceed four feet\n (4') at any point.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n There must be an adequate drainage system that removes floodwaters from the interior\n area of the crawlspace. The enclosed area should be drained within a reasonable time\n after a flood event.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The velocity of floodwaters at the site should not exceed five feet (5') per second\n for any crawlspace.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n See Technical Bulletin 11 for further information.\n

\n

\n Caution: Buildings that have below-grade crawlspaces will have higher flood insurance\n premiums than buildings that have the preferred crawlspace construction, with the\n interior elevation of the crawlspace soil at or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE).\n

\n

\n 10.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Other Development in Regulated Floodways:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Fences that have the potential to block the passage of floodwaters, such as stockade\n fences and wire mesh fences, in regulated floodways shall meet the limitations of\n subsection E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Retaining walls, bulkheads, sidewalks, and driveways that involve the placement of\n fill in regulated floodways shall meet the limitations of subsection E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Roads and watercourse crossings, including roads, bridges, culverts, low-water crossings,\n and similar means for vehicles or pedestrians to travel from one side of a watercourse\n to the other side, which encroach into regulated floodways, shall meet the limitations\n of subsection E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Drilling water, oil, and/or gas wells including fuel storage tanks, apparatus, and\n any equipment at the site that encroach into regulated floodways shall meet the limitations\n of subsection E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Docks, piers, boat ramps, marinas, moorings, decks, docking facilities, port facilities,\n shipbuilding, and ship repair facilities that encroach into regulated floodways shall\n meet the limitations of subsection E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n f.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Gravel and sand and their subsequent extraction on lands within the special flood\n hazard area that encroach into regulated floodways shall meet the limitations of subsection\n E of this section. A Reclamation Plan Bond for LOMR shall be posted by the mine/property\n owner with the City of Star to cover the estimated costs of a Reclamation LOMR as\n determined by the mine/property owner and shall provide supporting documentation for\n the estimated LOMR cost. A Reclamation LOMR shall be completed within one year of\n the completion of mining. Upon failure of the property owner to obtain a Reclamation\n LOMR of the mining site within one year, the Reclamation Plan Bond for LOMR will be\n forfeited.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 11.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Subdivision Plats: Flood Zones:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A note must be provided on the final plat documenting the current flood zone in which\n the property or properties are located. The boundary line must be drawn on the plat\n in situations where two (2) or more flood zones intersect over the property or properties\n being surveyed.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n FEMA FIRM panel(s): #160xxxxxxC, & 160xxxxxxE, etc.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n FIRM effective date(s): mm/dd/year\n

\n

\n Flood Zone(s): Zone X, Zone A, Zone AE, Zone AO, Zone AH, Zone D, etc.\n

\n

\n Base Flood Elevation(s): AE _____ .0 ft., etc.\n

\n

\n Flood Zones are subject to change by FEMA & all land within a floodway or floodplain\n is regulated by ____________ chapter/section of the City/County Code.\n

\n

\n 12.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Critical Facilities:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n As a best practice, FEMA recommends protection that exceeds code minimums. For example,\n FEMA 543, Design Guide for Improving Critical Facility Safety from Flooding and High\n Winds (2007) recommends protecting critical facilities to withstand at least a 0.2-percent-annual-chance\n flood event (often called the \"500-year flood event\"). Flood elevations for the 0.2-percent-annual-chance\n flood may be greater than the elevation specified by ASCE 24. If federal funding or\n other Federal action is involved, the requirements of Executive Order 11988 - Floodplain\n Management may necessitate protection of critical actions to the 500-year flood elevation\n (critical actions may include the construction and repair of critical facilities).\n

\n

\n In existing facilities that have not been substantially damaged, it may not be possible\n to floodproof or elevate to provide protection from the 0.2-percent-annual-chance\n flood event. In those instances, floodproofing or elevating as high as three feet\n (3') is recommended.\n

\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standards for Floodplains Without Established Base Flood Elevations: Within the special\n flood hazard areas designated as Zone A (also known as Unnumbered A Zones) and established\n in subsection 10-1-3B, where no base flood elevation (BFE) data has been provided\n by FEMA, the following provisions, in addition to the provisions of subsection A,\n shall apply:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The BFE used in determining the flood protection elevation (FPE) shall be determined\n based on the following criteria:\n

\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When base flood elevation (BFE) data is available from other sources, all new construction\n and substantial improvements within such areas shall also comply with all applicable\n provisions of this ordinance and shall be elevated or floodproofed in accordance with\n standards in subsections A and B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When floodway data is available from a Federal, State, or other source, all new construction\n and substantial improvements within floodway areas shall also comply with the requirements\n of subsection B and E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Require that all new subdivision proposals and other proposed developments (including\n proposals for manufactured home parks and subdivisions) greater than fifty (50) lots\n or five (5) acres, whichever is the lesser, include within such proposals base flood\n elevation data. Such base flood elevation (BFE) data shall be adopted by reference\n in accordance with subsection 10-1-3B and utilized in implementing this chapter. The\n applicant/developer shall submit an application for a Conditional Letter of Map Revision\n (CLOMR) prior to preliminary plat approval and have obtained a Letter of Map Revision\n (LOMR) prior to any building permits for structures being issued. (See FEMA 480 and/or\n FEMA 265 for further information.)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When base flood elevation (BFE) data is not available from a Federal, State, or other\n source as outlined above, the lowest floor shall be elevated or floodproofed (non-residential)\n to two feet (2') above the highest adjacent grade (HAG) at the building site or to\n the flood protection elevation (FPE) whichever is higher, as defined in section 10-1-2.\n All other applicable provisions of subsection B shall also apply.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standards for Riverine Floodplains with Base Flood Elevations but Without Established\n Floodways: Along rivers and streams where base flood elevation (BFE) data is provided\n by FEMA or is available from another source but floodways are not identified for a\n special flood hazard area on the FIRM or in the FIS report, the following requirements\n shall apply to all development within such areas:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standards of subsection A and B; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Until a regulatory floodway is designated, no encroachments, including fill, new construction,\n substantial improvements, or other development shall be permitted unless certification\n with supporting technical data by a registered professional engineer is provided demonstrating\n that the cumulative effect of the proposed development, when combined with all other\n existing and anticipated development, will not increase the water surface elevation\n of the base flood more than one foot (1') at any point within the community.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standards for Floodways: Areas designated as floodways located within the special\n flood hazard areas established in subsection 10-1-3B. The floodways are extremely\n hazardous areas due to the velocity of floodwaters that have erosion potential and\n carry debris and potential projectiles. The following provisions, in addition to standards\n outlined in subsections A and B, shall apply to all development within such areas:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements, and\n other developments shall be permitted unless:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n It is demonstrated that the proposed encroachment would not result in any increase\n in the flood levels during the occurrence of the base flood, based on hydrologic and\n hydraulic analyses performed in accordance with standard engineering practice and\n presented to the Floodplain Administrator prior to issuance of floodplain development\n permit (This is a no-rise analysis and certification); or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A Conditional Letter of Map Revision (CLOMR) has been approved by FEMA. A Letter of\n Map Revision (LOMR) must also be obtained within six (6) months of completion of the\n proposed encroachment.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If subsection E1 is satisfied, all development shall comply with all applicable flood\n hazard reduction provisions of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Manufactured homes may be permitted provided the following provisions are met:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The anchoring and the elevation standards of subsection B3; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The encroachment standards of subsection E1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n F.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standards for Areas of Shallow Flooding (Zone AO, AH, AR/AO, or AR/AH): Areas designated\n as shallow flooding areas have special flood hazards associated with base flood depths\n of one feet (1') to three feet (3') where a clearly defined channel does not exist\n and where the path of flooding is unpredictable and indeterminate. In addition to\n subsections A and B, all new construction and substantial improvements shall meet\n the following requirements:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The lowest floor shall be elevated at least as high as the depth number specified\n on the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM), in feet, plus a freeboard of two feet (2'),\n above the highest adjacent grade; or at least four feet (4') above the highest adjacent\n grade if no depth number is specified.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Non-residential structures may, in lieu of elevation, be floodproofed to the same\n level as required in subsection F1 so that the structure, together with attendant\n utility and sanitary facilities, below that level shall be watertight with walls substantially\n impermeable to the passage of water and with structural components having the capability\n of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and effects of buoyancy. Certification\n is required in accordance with subsection B2 and subsection 10-1-4C3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Accessory Structure (Appurtenant Structure) (Sheds, Detached Garages, Etc.):\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Used solely for parking, access, and storage:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Shall have the lowest floor elevated at least as high as the depth number specified\n on the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM), in feet, plus a freeboard of two feet (2'),\n above the highest adjacent grade; or at least four feet (4') above the highest adjacent\n grade if no depth number is specified; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (2)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Shall have flood openings to facilitate automatic equalization of hydrostatic flood\n forces shall be provided below flood protection elevation in conformance with the\n provisions of subsection A8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Not used solely for parking, access, and storage:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (1)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Shall be elevated per subsections B1 and B2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Adequate drainage paths shall be provided around structures on slopes to guide floodwaters\n around and away from proposed structures.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":false,"CompareStatus":4,"DocOrderId":665,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT10FLCO","NodeDepth":3,"TitleHtml":"
10-1-6: - Legal Status Provisions
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT10FLCO_CH1FLOR_10-1-6LESTPR","Title":"10-1-6: - Legal Status Provisions","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Effect on Rights and Liabilities Under the Existing Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance:\n This chapter, in part, comes forward by re-enactment of some of the provisions of\n the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance enacted September 6, 2002 as amended, and it\n is not the intention to repeal but rather to re-enact and continue to enforce without\n interruption of such existing provisions, so that all rights and liabilities that\n have accrued thereunder are reserved and may be enforced. The enactment of this chapter\n shall not affect any action, suit, or proceeding instituted or pending. All provisions\n of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance of the City of Star enacted on September\n 6, 2002, as amended, which are not reenacted herein are repealed.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Effect upon Outstanding Floodplain Development Permits: Nothing herein contained shall\n require any change in the plans, construction, size, or designated use of any development\n or any part thereof for which a Floodplain Development Permit has been granted by\n the Floodplain Administrator or his or her authorized agents before the time of passage\n of this chapter. Provided, however, that when construction is not begun under such\n outstanding permit within a period of one hundred eighty (180) days subsequent to\n the date of issuance of the outstanding permit, construction or use shall be in conformity\n with the provisions of this chapter.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Severability: This chapter is hereby declared to be severable. Should any portion\n of this chapter be declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining\n provisions shall continue in full force and effect and shall be read to carry out\n the purpose(s) of the chapter before the declaration of partial invalidity.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. 336, 5-4-2021)\n
